Lots to learn, cool office, but overall oppressive environment, crappy code and poor management. Great office building,

-Generally very crowded and cramped work environment.  Everyone sits right on top of each other, and so there is plenty of distraction.  When people get sick, everyone gets sick.  The elevator banks were worse than the 6 train below the building during rush hour.

text: glad I was here, glad I'm gone Some very talented and helpful people on the team. Generous pension, good benefits. Recently upgraded IT systems. Option to occasionally work from home. No micro-management - not necessarily a good thing when trying to learn the ropes, but a great environment to develop, learn new skills and carve out your own niche within the firm. Hard work and achievement are recognised and praised.  (However, recognition may not translate into career progression if you're not bringing in big £££.) The right person could go far here, but a lot comes down to personality. Old-fashioned chivalry! Women always enter and exit the lifts first :) Every department has to justify its existence, with success measured in fees earned - including for work done internally, which creates a barrier to collaboration. Hot-desking on tiny desks, outsourced IT, extremely limited facilities for employees (no kitchen or dining facilities to speak of) - I often felt like a cog in the machine. A lot of processes are rather ad hoc, with very little standardisation (despite efforts by some team members!). No real sense of direction. Strategic hires of high-level personnel, but little concern for lower-down, back-office staff. While many people on the team are extremely talented and committed, some are not - and unfortunately a half-assed approach is tolerated when accompanied by the right personality.
